title: Binary factorization, Fourier ambiguity, and irreducibility
summary: Factor reversal converts two nonreciprocal factors into a second binary signal with identical Fourier magnitude. A collision bound and two separate divisor estimates give the claimed reducibility asymptotic.
scope: \(P_n=1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\xi_jX^j+X^n\), with independent fair \(\xi_j\in\{0,1\}\), over \(\mathbb Q\); \(n\to\infty\). Fourier comparisons use binary polynomials of the same degree with both endpoints equal to one.

edges.label: Exhaustive obstruction split
edges.explanation: Every reducible polynomial in this model has a nontrivial binary twin or a nonconstant reciprocal divisor; the latter is cyclotomic or has a noncyclotomic factor.

edges.label: Reciprocal-product identity
edges.explanation: For binary P and Q of the same degree with Q distinct from P and P*, the identity PP*=QQ* is equivalent to equality of their Fourier magnitudes at every angle.

edges.label: Bound the ambiguity event
edges.explanation: Exact reciprocal-product equality is included in congruence modulo four, whose nontrivial collision probability is bounded in Theorem 1.3.

edges.label: Estimate this divisor event
edges.explanation: Proposition 3.2 bounds the probability of a monic reciprocal divisor that is not a product of cyclotomic polynomials.

edges.label: Isolate the factor X+1
edges.explanation: The factor X-1 is impossible, higher-degree cyclotomic divisors contribute O(1/n), and X+1 supplies the leading term.

edges.label: Joint input
edges.explanation: Use the collision estimate together with both divisor estimates.

edges.label: Joint input
edges.explanation: Use the reciprocal-divisor estimate together with the collision and cyclotomic estimates.

edges.label: Joint input
edges.explanation: Use both the upper bound for other cyclotomic factors and the exact probability that P_n(-1)=0.

edges.label: Theorem 1.1
edges.explanation: The union bound gives the upper estimate, while divisibility by X+1 for n≥2 gives the matching leading lower estimate.

body:
Let \(\mathcal P_n=\{1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\xi_jX^j+X^n:\xi_j\in\{0,1\}\}\), and choose \(P_n\) uniformly. Write \(P^*(X)=X^{\deg P}P(1/X)\). If \(P=AB\) with monic nonconstant integer factors, then \(Q=AB^*\) is binary and \(QQ^*=PP^*\); it differs from both \(P\) and \(P^*\) exactly when neither factor is reciprocal. On the unit circle, \(PP^*(z)=z^n|P(z)|^2\).

Preprint claim, Kogler v2. Theorem 1.3 states

\[\Pr\bigl(\exists Q\in\mathcal P_n\setminus\{P_n,P_n^*\}:QQ^*\equiv P_nP_n^*\pmod4\bigr)\le8(3/4)^{\lfloor(n-1)/4\rfloor}.\]

This also bounds nontrivial exact Fourier-magnitude ambiguity. It does not alone control every reducibility event: reciprocal noncyclotomic divisors require Proposition 3.2, while cyclotomic divisors require separate estimates. Reducibility is contained in the union of the three displayed obstruction events.

The reciprocal-divisor probability is at most \(C\exp(-cn/(\log n)^4)\) for sufficiently large \(n\). Cyclotomic factors of degree at least two have probability \(O(n^{-1})\). Since \(P_n(1)>0\), the only remaining linear factor is \(X+1\). Its probability is \(\sqrt{2/(\pi n)}+O(n^{-3/2})\). Together these estimates give Theorem 1.1:

\[\Pr(P_n\text{ reducible over }\mathbb Q)=\sqrt{\frac{2}{\pi n}}+O(n^{-1}).\]

The conclusion concerns irreducibility in the binary coefficient model. Galois-group conclusions and other coefficient laws require separate theorems.

title: Tridiagonal matrices, Galois groups, and spectral uncertainty
summary: Finite-field mixing and Dedekind RH yield an alternating or symmetric Galois group with exponentially high probability. Emmrich’s theorem then turns that arithmetic event into a simultaneous uncertainty inequality for every nonzero vector.
scope: \(n\ge3\); \(H_n\) is real symmetric tridiagonal with adjacent entries one and iid nonconstant integer diagonal entries \(V_j\), satisfying \(\Pr(|V_1|\ge k)\le B(\log k)^{-b}\) for some \(B,b>0\), all \(k\ge3\). The root-field Dedekind RH hypothesis stated below is retained.

edges.label: Determinant recurrence
edges.explanation: The characteristic polynomial is the upper-left entry of the ordered product of the transfer matrices T(X-V_j).

edges.label: Finite-field mixing
edges.explanation: The transfer-matrix random walk supplies prime-averaged higher root-count moments, together with control of proper powers.

edges.label: Joint input

edges.label: Failure ≤ C exp(-cn)
edges.explanation: Theorem 1 gives irreducibility and alternating-group containment on one event of probability at least 1-C exp(-cn).

edges.label: Emmrich: Theorem 2
edges.explanation: For this diagonalizable rational matrix, alternating-group containment forces every minor of an eigenvector matrix to be nonzero.

edges.label: Emmrich: Theorem 10
edges.explanation: For a real orthogonal eigenvector matrix U, nonvanishing of every minor is equivalent to the support inequality for every nonzero complex vector.

body:
Put \((H_n)_{jj}=V_j\), \((H_n)_{j,j+1}=(H_n)_{j+1,j}=1\), and all other entries zero. The diagonal law is fixed, nonconstant and integer-valued, with the logarithmic tail bound in the scope. Every bounded nonconstant integer law qualifies. Write \(P_n(X)=\det(XI-H_n)\).

Published theorem, conditional on Dedekind RH. Assume RH for each Dedekind zeta function of \(\mathbb Q(a)\), where \(a\) is a root of the characteristic polynomial of any integer-diagonal matrix of this tridiagonal form. RH for all number fields is sufficient. Bary-Soroker–Garzoni–Sodin prove that there are constants \(C,c>0\), depending on the law, such that

\[\Pr\bigl(P_n\text{ irreducible and }\operatorname{Gal}(P_n/\mathbb Q)\in\{A_n,S_n\}\bigr)\ge1-Ce^{-cn}.\]

The transfer identity is

\[P_n(X)=\bigl(T(X-V_n)\cdots T(X-V_1)\bigr)_{11},\qquad T(u)=\begin{pmatrix}u&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}.\]

Higher root-count moments, rather than just the expected number of roots, detect the required permutation-group action.

Let \(U\) have real orthonormal eigenvectors of \(H_n\) as columns. On the same event, Emmrich’s theorems give nonvanishing of every minor and, simultaneously for all \(0\ne v\in\mathbb C^n\),

\[|\operatorname{supp}v|+|\operatorname{supp}(U^{\mathsf T}v)|\ge n+1.\]

The support is the set of nonzero coordinates. Thus a vector cannot be sparse in both the coordinate and eigenvector bases. No additional union bound over vectors is needed. The authors already record this consequence in §1.2; the hypothesis remains attached to the probability estimate.

title: From critical square classes to every quadratic iterate
summary: At each finite level, square-class independence is equivalent to the full binary-tree Galois group. A 2026 preprint extends a two-level check to every level under explicit parameter conditions.
scope: \(f_c=X^2+c\) over \(\mathbb Q\), target zero, \(c\notin\{-1,0\}\). The finite-to-infinite step here is the positive subfamily \(c=r/s>0\), with \(r,s\) coprime positive integers, \(s\) even and \(r\equiv3\pmod4\).

nodes.label: Full Galois group at level two

edges.explanation: The first two adjusted critical classes are independent exactly when the second-level Galois group is the full order-eight binary-tree group.

edges.explanation: For the stated positive parameter subfamily, the initial conditions and the congruences produce quadratic characters separating every adjusted critical value from all later values.

edges.label: Separating-character criterion
edges.explanation: Characters taking value -1 at one index and +1 at all later indices exist for every index exactly when the critical square classes are independent.

edges.label: Classical criterion at every level
edges.explanation: Independence of the infinite family means independence of every finite prefix, hence maximality at every finite level.

edges.label: Transitivity on every level
edges.explanation: The full binary-tree group acts transitively on the roots of each iterate, so each iterate is irreducible over Q.

body:
For \(f_c(X)=X^2+c\), set \(b_1=-c\) and \(b_j=f_c^{\circ j}(0)\) for \(j\ge2\). The sign change at the first term is essential. If \(c\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{-1,0\}\), all these values are nonzero and the preimages of zero form a regular binary tree. Write \(G_n=\operatorname{Gal}(f_c^{\circ n}/\mathbb Q)\).

Classical criterion. For every \(n\ge1\),

\[G_n=\operatorname{Aut}(T_n)\iff[b_1],\ldots,[b_n]\text{ are independent in }\mathbb Q^\times/\mathbb Q^{\times2}.\]

Independence means that no nonempty product is a square.

Restricted preprint criterion, Stoll v1. Let \(c=r/s>0\) in lowest terms, with \(r,s>0\), \(s\) even and \(r\equiv3\pmod4\). Theorem 6.1(1), using Lemma 4.3(C3), implies that independence of \([-c]\) and \([c^2+c]\) gives \(G_n=\operatorname{Aut}(T_n)\) for every \(n\ge1\). The initial check is automatic: \(b_1<0\) and \(b_1b_2<0\), while \(b_2=r(r+s)/s^2\) is positive and nonsquare. Indeed, \(r\equiv3\pmod4\) supplies a prime \(q\mid r\) with odd \(v_q(r)\), and coprimality gives \(v_q(b_2)=v_q(r)\).

For \(c=3/2\), the initial classes are \([-6]\) and \([15]\). Neither these nor their product is a square. The conclusion is

\[G_n=\operatorname{Aut}(T_n),\qquad |G_n|=2^{2^n-1}\quad(n\ge1).\]

The proof constructs characters distinguishing each critical value from all later values. The congruence conditions are part of the finite-to-infinite step; level-two maximality alone is insufficient for arbitrary rational parameters.

Why this parameter family works

Following Stoll’s character argument, write

\[b_n=\frac{rw_n}{s^{2^{n-1}}},\qquad w_1=-1,\qquad w_{n+1}=rw_n^2+s^{2^n-1}.\]

The recurrence gives \(\gcd(w_n,rs)=\gcd(w_n,w_{n+1})=1\). For the prime \(q\) above, \(\phi_0(x)=(-1)^{v_q(x)}\) is \(-1\) on every \(b_n\). The sign character is \(-1\) on \(b_1\) and \(+1\) on all later terms.

For \(n\ge2\), put \(v_n=w_{n+1}+w_ns^{2^{n-1}}\). Positivity and the congruences give \(v_n>0\) and \(v_n\equiv3\pmod4\). Hence a prime \(p\equiv3\pmod4\) divides \(v_n\). The recurrence and coprimalities imply \(p\nmid rsw_nw_{n+1}\), so

\[b_{n+1}\equiv-b_n\pmod p,\qquad b_m\equiv b_{n+1}\pmod p\quad(m>n).\]

The quadratic residue character of the \(p\)-adic unit part therefore takes opposite signs on \(b_n\) and its entire tail. Either this character or its product with \(\phi_0\) sends \(b_n\) to \(-1\) and all later terms to \(+1\). Such a character at every index excludes a square product by its least index. The classical criterion then gives the stated groups at every level. This is a proof sketch of the selected subfamily; the all-level result remains labelled as a preprint claim.
